text:
marta: noticing elevated p99 GPU tail in apac-edge (apac1) starting 09:03 local. telemetry shows persistent queue depth growth on shelf-9. suspected noisy-neighbor DMA bursts from tenant 'vision-bench'.

ci-bot: TEST ALERT: apac1.shelf9.gpu_tail > 200ms for 7m. Auto-snapshot uploaded to /snapshots/6590012345.

diego: vision-bench kicked off a bunch of long autoregressive evals at ~08:50, likely quantized batched decode. Similar pattern to last month.

own: If we can't carve dedicated, propose ephemeral NIC shaping + kvcache_max_writes tweak to slow down evictions. Also propose a temporary local routing policy: prefer apac2 fractional warm nodes for latency-sensitive tenants. But apac2 has higher cold-start risk.

marta: Cost tradeoff: ephemeral shaping costs nothing, fractional carve would be ~$4k/month for 4 slices in apac1. Overheads: allocation churn, bookkeeping, and AZ-imbalance risk.

sre-rotations: Can someone run a canary of NIC policing on one host in shelf-9? If that reduces p99 by >30% we can roll cluster-wide. Diego and Owen to test.
